issues.title: Missing private modifier on gleanWrapper
issues.description: The rule requires that properties have explicit access control modifiers with 'private' for implementation details. The gleanWrapper property lacks the 'private' modifier, exposing an internal implementation detail that should not be accessible outside the struct.
issues.rule_name: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

issues.title: Incorrect Reader Mode URL handling in cancelEditMode
issues.description: The cancelEditMode function now incorrectly preserves reader mode URLs when canceling edit mode. The logic was changed from '&&' (AND) to '||' (OR), which means reader mode URLs will now be kept instead of being cleared. This breaks the expected behavior where reader mode URLs should be filtered out when canceling URL editing, potentially causing the address bar to display internal reader:// URLs to users instead of the original webpage URL.

issues.title: Inverted reader mode telemetry state tracking
issues.description: The recordReaderModeTelemetry function has inverted logic for determining reader mode state. When the reader mode is 'available' (about to be enabled), it reports false instead of true, and for all other states it reports true instead of false. This causes telemetry data to incorrectly track reader mode usage patterns - reporting that reader mode is being disabled when it's actually being enabled and vice versa. This will corrupt analytics data about reader mode feature usage.

issues.title: Wrong display view type for reader mode action
issues.description: The handleShowReaderModeAction function sets the wrong displayView type when the user taps the reader mode button. Instead of setting displayView to '.readerMode' (which would show the reader mode view), it's set to '.readerModeLongPressAction' (which is meant for long-press actions). This causes the wrong UI component to be displayed when users try to activate reader mode, breaking the core reader mode functionality and showing an incorrect action sheet instead of the reader view.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31577 - Remove FXIOS-14593 [BVC] Clean up qr code related code from BVC
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
The PR removes the QR-code scanner entry point from the browser: the `qrCode` toolbar action, the `showQRCode` route and `QRCode` quick-action/deeplink cases, the `QRCodeViewControllerDelegate` conformance on BrowserViewController, the `qrCode` display state, and the Glean probes for QR scan and QR button taps. The removal is mostly clean: I grepped the head tree and found no dangling references to the removed cases, and the QR scanner itself stays in place because FxA sign-in, onboarding, settings, and remote tabs still use it.

The PR also contains three behavior changes that have nothing to do with QR codes and are not mentioned in the description. The most serious is in `BrowserViewControllerState.handleShowReaderModeAction`, where the display state changed from `.readerMode` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. `showReaderMode` is the action dispatched by a plain tap on the reader-mode toolbar button and by the main menu. After this change, that tap runs `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, which adds the page to the reading list, instead of `toggleReaderMode()`, which enables or disables reader mode. The reader-mode telemetry boolean is also inverted, and `cancelEditMode` had its reader-mode check flipped from `&&` to `||`. None of these three changes is covered by a test, and the PR's unit-test checkbox is unchecked.

Overall the removal is sound, but the PR should not merge as-is. The reader-mode regression is a user-facing break in core toolbar functionality, and the other two unrelated edits need to be reverted or justified separately.
structured_output.verdictRationale: One critical regression: tapping the reader-mode button (and the matching main-menu item) now routes to the add-to-reading-list handler instead of toggling reader mode, because `handleShowReaderModeAction` was switched to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. Two further undocumented logic changes (inverted reader-mode telemetry, flipped `cancelEditMode` condition) and a telemetry-counter removal that still affects a live QR path need to be fixed or justified. The QR removal itself is clean.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, the address bar toolbar (`ToolbarMiddleware`) dispatches `GeneralBrowserAction`s to `BrowserViewControllerState`, a reducer that maps each action to a `DisplayType`. `BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions` then turns that display type into a concrete UI call. QR scanning was one of these display types. It was reached from the toolbar's `qrCode` button, the `QRCode` home-screen quick action and deeplink, and the `showQRCode` route, and it was also the `QRCodeViewControllerDelegate` that BrowserViewController implemented.

This PR removes the BVC-side of that path: the toolbar action case, the `showQRCode` route and `QRCode` shortcut/deeplink cases, the `qrCodeReader` display state, the QR delegate methods on BVC, and the QR Glean metrics. The QR scanner infrastructure (`QRCodeCoordinator`, `QRCodeViewController`, `QRCodeNavigationHandler`) stays because FxA sign-in still uses it. The PR also reroutes the reader-mode display state, and that reroute is where the regression sits.
steps: Entry point: the address toolbar in `ToolbarMiddleware.didTapButton` and `didLongPressButton` converts a tap or long-press on a button into a `GeneralBrowserAction`. The `readerMode` button tap dispatches `showReaderMode`, and its long-press dispatches `addToReadingListLongPressAction`.

Removed path: the `qrCode` button case, the `showQRCode` route in `Route.AppAction`, the `QRCode` cases in `DeeplinkInput.Shortcut`, `ShortcutType`, and `RouteBuilder`, plus the QR delegate and `handleQRCode` on `BrowserViewController`. Nothing in the head tree still references them.

Reducer change: `BrowserViewControllerState.handleShowReaderModeAction` now sets `displayView` to `.readerModeLongPressAction` instead of `.readerMode`. Because `handleDisplayActions` routes `.readerModeLongPressAction` to `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, the reader-mode tap now runs the add-to-reading-list path, and the `.readerMode` display state has no producers left.
Telemetry change: `recordReaderModeTelemetry` in `ToolbarMiddleware` flips the `isEnabled` boolean, so the reported state is inverted relative to what the tap will do.

Metrics change: the `qr_code.scanned` counter and the `qr_scan_button_tapped` event are removed from the probes and the `TelemetryWrapper` mapping. QR scanning still runs through FxA sign-in, which does not record that counter.

findings.title: Reader-mode tap now adds to reading list instead of toggling reader mode
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/BrowserViewController/State/BrowserViewControllerState.swift`, `handleShowReaderModeAction` (around line 566) was changed from `displayView: .readerMode` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. That breaks the reader-mode toolbar and main-menu tap, because `BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions` sends `.readerModeLongPressAction` to `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, which adds the page to reading list. Restore `.readerMode` in that function so it routes to `toggleReaderMode()` again. Leave `handleAddToReadingListLongPressAction` unchanged, since it already maps to `.readerModeLongPressAction` correctly. Then add a reducer test in `BrowserViewControllerState` tests that asserts `showReaderMode` produces `.readerMode`. Keep the `.readerMode` case in `BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions`.

findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry boolean is inverted
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/Redux/ToolbarMiddleware.swift`, `recordReaderModeTelemetry` (around lines 520-530) inverts the `isReaderModeEnabled` value. Before this PR, `.available` mapped to `true`, since a tap on an available state enables reader mode, and `default` mapped to `false`. Restore that mapping. This PR's other change to the same function is not part of this fix. Add a unit test in `ToolbarMiddlewareTests` that verifies `readerModeButtonTapped` records `isEnabled: true` for `.available` and `false` for `.active`, using the existing `mockGleanWrapper`.

findings.title: Unexplained `cancelEditMode` condition flip exposes reader-mode URL on cancel
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/Redux/ToolbarMiddleware.swift`, `cancelEditMode(windowUUID:)` (around line 485) was changed from `isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL` to `isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL`. The PR's stated scope is QR-code removal, so this change is unrelated. Revert it to the original `&&` / `!isReaderModeURL` condition unless the author can confirm the new behavior is intended. If it is intended, move it to its own change with a description and a test that checks the URL passed in the cancelEdit action for a reader-mode page.

findings.title: No tests cover the behavior changes in this PR
findings.body:
The PR removes QR tests, and that is the only test work it does. The checklist item "I ensured unit tests pass and wrote tests for new code" is unchecked. Three behavior changes ship without coverage:

- `showReaderMode` now produces `.readerModeLongPressAction`, and no reducer test catches it.
- The reader-mode telemetry `isEnabled` mapping is untested, so the inversion went unnoticed.
- The `cancelEditMode` condition change has no test.

The existing `ToolbarMiddlewareTests` only assert dispatched action types, so they would still pass with all three bugs in place.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Toolbar/ToolbarMiddlewareTests.swift" lines="308-313"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add tests for the reader-mode behavior touched by this PR. In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Toolbar/ToolbarMiddlewareTests.swift`, add a test that checks `readerModeButtonTapped` records `isEnabled` true when `readerModeState` is `.available` and false when `.active`, using `mockGleanWrapper`. Add a `cancelEdit` test for a reader-mode URL, and a `BrowserViewControllerState` reducer test that asserts `showReaderMode` yields `displayView == .readerMode`. Follow the style of the existing `didTapButton` tests in the same file.

findings.title: QR scan counter removed while QR scanning remains reachable from FxA
findings.fixPrompt: The PR removes the `qr_code.scanned` counter from `firefox-ios/Client/Glean/probes/metrics.yaml` and the matching `TelemetryWrapper` mapping. QR scanning still runs through FxA sign-in (`RustFxA/FirefoxAccountSignInViewController.swift`), which doesn't record that counter. Confirm with the data stewards that losing this signal is acceptable, or keep the counter and record it from the FxA scan path. Add a note to the PR description so the data review covers this removal.

findings.title: Unrelated version bump in a QR-removal PR
findings.body:
`version.xcconfig` changes `APP_VERSION` from 147.1 to 147.2. This is a release-train change, not part of the QR cleanup. Mixing it in makes this PR harder to revert and muddles the changelog. Move it into its own release commit or PR.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Client/Configuration/version.xcconfig" lines="1-1"}
findings.fixPrompt: Remove the `APP_VERSION` change from `firefox-ios/Client/Configuration/version.xcconfig`. Keep it at 147.1 in this PR and let the release process bump the version separately.

findings.title: QR removal is cleanly scoped and leaves no dangling references
findings.body: The removal is consistent across the routing layers. `ShortcutType.qrCode`, `DeeplinkInput.Shortcut.qrCode`, `Route.AppAction.showQRCode`, and the `RouteBuilder` case are all gone together. `ToolbarActionConfiguration.qrCode` and `ToolbarMiddleware`'s handler are gone too. A grep of the head tree finds no remaining references to these identifiers outside the still-live QR scanner code. Because `makeRoute` returns `nil` for unknown shortcut types, a stale `QRCode` quick action would be a harmless no-op. No plist-declared static shortcut references it.

findings.title: QR scanner infrastructure correctly kept for FxA sign-in
findings.body: The PR removes only the BVC-side QR path. `QRCodeCoordinator`, `QRCodeViewController`, `QRCodeNavigationHandler`, and `BrowserCoordinator.showQRCode` remain. They are still used by FxA sign-in, onboarding, settings, and remote tabs, and `BrowserViewController` still hands `navigationHandler` to FxA sign-in as its `qrCodeNavigationHandler`. Keeping the scanner is the right scope for this PR. A follow-up could clean up the other entry points, but it should not remove that shared code without first moving those flows off it.
